requirements:
Component: a printed plastic part, a tube closed at its top with two opposed stubs on bosses, tested in tension on a universal testing machine by its stubs.

Geometry (CAD): metres. The part in the STEP file is a tube along z, closed at its top, with two opposed stubs of diameter 15.3 mm on bosses along x, axis at y = 0, z = 30.59 mm. Both stubs were lengthened by 40 mm for gripping (same diameter and axis), so the part spans x from -74.85 to 74.85 mm; the added lengths run from x = -74.85 to -34.85 mm and from x = 34.85 to 74.85 mm.

Material: Formlabs Rigid 10K resin, printed and post-cured; linear elastic and isotropic, E = 10 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.35.

Service loads (the test): the machine's moving grip pulls the +x stub along +x with a total force of 300 N. The pull reaches the part through the grip's jaws, which hold the whole added length of the +x stub (x from 34.85 to 74.85 mm) all round and spread the pull evenly over that surface.

Installation and supports (the test machine): both grips are wedge grips aligned on the machine's axis, which is the stubs' axis. The jaws of the stationary grip hold the whole added length of the -x stub (x from -74.85 to -34.85 mm) all round and do not move at all. The jaws of the moving grip hold the added length of the +x stub; they travel only along the machine's axis, so that surface is pulled along x but cannot move sideways (in y or z). The stub end faces and the rest of the part touch nothing.

Analysis scope: static, linear elastic, small deformations, no gravity; a solid (three-dimensional) model of the whole part.

Required result: ext_marks = ux(B) - ux(A), the x-elongation between the video-extensometer marks A = (-27, 7.656, 30.588) mm and B = (27, 7.656, 30.588) mm on the front of the original stubs, in m.

mapping.implied_by: The stationary grip's jaws hold the -x stub's added length all round and do not move.
The moving grip travels only along the machine's axis: that surface cannot move sideways.
